headline: NAB's credit impairment charge (CIC) rose $105m or 14.4% to $833m in FY25 (12 months to Sep 2025) from $728m in FY24. The FY25 charge comprises individually assessed charges of $964m and a $131m release from collective provisions. The credit impairment charge to GLAs (annualised) rose 1 bp to 0.11% from 0.10%. By division (net charge, Sep25 vs Sep24): Corporate & Institutional Banking +$153m (146 vs a write-back of 7); Corporate Functions and Other +$83m (write-back 122 vs 205); Business & Private Banking +$6m (529 vs 523); Personal Banking -$33m (255 vs 288); New Zealand Banking -$104m (25 vs 129). The divisional deltas sum to +$105m, matching the total.

drivers.narrative: Individually assessed charge rose $328m (51.6%) to $964m from $636m: new and increased +$329m to $1,192m, write-backs -$46m to $178m, recoveries -$45m to $50m. Driven by higher C&IB charge for impairment of a small number of customers plus non-recurrence of prior-year write-backs/recoveries, and modest increases in B&PB and NZ business lending and Personal unsecured retail.

Collective swung from a $92m charge to a $131m write-back (-$223m). Driven by a net release of forward-looking provisions (incl. $283m FLA release) and release of provisions for customers transferred to individually assessed, partially offset by volume growth in B&PB business lending and asset quality deterioration across the Australian lending portfolio.

limitations: The collective driver is a single net number (-$223m); the bank does not publish separate quantified splits for its forward-looking release, volume growth and asset-quality components, so these are described narratively (the $283m FLA release is stated in the CEO review).
The divisional impairment charges are net (individually assessed plus collective) and are presented as the where-layer; they do not map one-to-one onto the provision-type drivers.
The investor presentation divisional charts are half-yearly (context) and were used only to corroborate the FY levels; the results book divisional tables are the authoritative source.
The C&IB FY24 figure is a write-back of $7m (shown as a positive 7 in the results table), so its +$153m delta is computed from a charge of 146 against a write-back of 7.

evidence_records.quote: Collective credit impairment charge decreased by $223 million from a charge of $92 million to a write-back of $131 million. The write-back for the September 2025 full year of $131 million was driven by a net release of forward-looking provisions, combined with the release of provisions held for customers that transferred to individually assessed during the September 2025 full year. This was partially offset by the impact of volume growth in the Business and Private Banking business lending portfolio, combined with deterioration in asset quality across the Australian lending portfolio.
